newsitem.title: UK: Business calm on London sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Business calm on London sugar freight market.

text.p: London's sugar freight market was subdued on Tuesday with little new business reported from Santos and one new order from the tail-end of the Thai crop, shipbrokers said on Tuesday.
CSR quoted for 40,000 tonnes of bulk sugar from Queensland to Adabiya for August 10/20 and a further 20,000 tonnes to Savannah/Gramercy for August 13/23.
Genoc was in the market for a prompt 14/20,000 tonnes in bulk from Thailand to Vladivostok or Novorossisk.
Shipbrokers cited talk of a possible Glencore order for 12/14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar from Thailand to the Black Sea/Red Sea/east Africa plus other options for July/August dates.
Firmer business was thin on the ground with only two fixtures reported.
Fiji Sugar Marketing fixed 18,000 tonnes from Fiji to Savannah/Gramercy for August 5/15 and E D & F Man fixed a prompt 14,000-tonne bagged cargo from Santos to Lagos.

Elsewhere, market sources said Syria was likely to retender this week to buy 26,000 tonnes of white and raw sugar after two previous cancellations. The cargoes were originally scheduled for delivery in August.
